name: Rasterization and GPU Shaders
text:
# Rasterization and GPU Shaders

Also called: GPU-based Voxelization, Shader-based Voxelization

## Overview
This family converts triangle meshes into discrete volumetric representations (voxels) by leveraging GPU hardware rasterization pipelines or programmable shaders, rather than CPU-based geometric intersection tests. It solves the problem of real-time or high-throughput [voxelization](#12-voxelization.md) for volume rendering and fluid simulation by mapping 2D rasterization concepts or explicit geometry generation to 3D grid occupancy [S1, S2, unofficial]. It differs from sibling methods like [Voxel Carving](1213-voxel-carving.md) or [Implicit Surface Voxelization](2379-implicit-surface-voxelization.md) by relying on the graphics pipeline's fragment processing or [geometry shaders](#4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) to determine voxel inclusion, often producing explicit cube meshes or point clouds rather than dense occupancy grids [S1, S4, S3, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family map a conceptual or physical source into a discrete or analytic volumetric representation suitable for rendering [G]. The core mechanism involves:
1. **Domain Definition**: Establishing a spatial domain, typically a 3D grid with resolution $(N_x, N_y, N_z)$ and bounding box, or an infinite analytic space [G].
2. **Value Assignment**: Determining the value (density, distance, color) for each point in the domain based on the source method (geometric intersection, function evaluation, or physical state) [G].
3. **Storage/Access**: Either storing the result in a discrete array (voxelization, simulation) or providing an interface to compute it on-the-fly (procedural) [G].

## Subtopics

### [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md)
A technique that converts a triangle mesh into a discrete volumetric representation by projecting the geometry onto a 3D grid using hardware rasterization principles or hash-based spatial mapping. It solves the problem of generating surface-level voxel data ([shell voxelization](#1748-shell-based-voxelization.md)) for volume rendering or voxel art, differing from CPU-based geometric intersection methods by leveraging efficient [spatial hashing](#5002-spatial-hashing.md) or GPU fragment shaders to determine voxel occupancy. Unlike [3D Grid Rasterization](903-3d-grid-rasterization.md) which outputs a dense or sparse occupancy grid, this method often generates explicit cube mesh geometry or point clouds from the occupied voxels.

### [Mesh-to-Voxel Geometry Shader](2800-mesh-to-voxel-geometry-shader.md)
A real-time technique that converts mesh geometry into discrete voxel-like cubes by iterating over integer grid positions within a triangle's bounding box and emitting cube geometry for positions close to the triangle plane. Unlike [rasterization-based voxelization](#908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) which fills pixels, this method explicitly generates cube geometry for every grid cell intersecting the triangle, resulting in significantly higher vertex and triangle counts.

### Instanced Voxelization
#### definition
A technique to draw all voxelization slices in a single draw call using instancing [S1, unofficial].
#### step
Use instancing to draw all slices in a single draw call. Use the instance ID to specify the target slice [S1, unofficial].

### Rasterization-based Voxelization Shader
#### definition
A fragment shader that rasterizes geometry into a 3D grid volume by mapping clip-space coordinates to grid indices and writing a value to a structured buffer [S2, unofficial].
#### step
Extract clip-space position: `float3 xyz = i.vertex.xyz;` [S2, unofficial]. Handle reversed Z if applicable: `#if defined(UNITY_REVERSED_Z) xyz.z = 1 - xyz.z; #endif` [S2, unofficial]. Scale and clamp to grid resolution: `xyz.z *= _CVCT_GridResolutionI * 0.99999;` [S2, unofficial]. Convert to integer grid coordinates: `int3 pos = int3(xyz);` [S2, unofficial]. Calculate flat index: `int index = dot(pos, int3(1, _CVCT_GridResolutionI, _CVCT_GridResolutionI * _CVCT_GridResolutionI));` [S2, unofficial]. Write to buffer: `_CVCT_gv[index] = 1;` [S2, unofficial].
#### parameter
`_CVCT_GridResolutionI`: integer resolution of the grid, used for coordinate scaling and indexing [S2, unofficial].
#### layout
`_CVCT_gv`: `RWStructuredBuffer<int>` storing grid values [S2, unofficial].
#### pitfall
Coordinate mapping: The shader multiplies Z by 0.99999 to ensure $0 \le pos.z < GridResolution$, preventing out-of-bounds writes due to floating-point precision errors at the boundary [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The use of GPU shaders for voxelization emerged with the availability of stream output and geometry shaders in the mid-2000s. Blythe (2006) described stream output as a mechanism to cache transformed vertices, allowing deforming meshes (like skinned characters) to be voxelized without recomputing transformations for each slice [S1, unofficial]. This approach was adopted in real-time fluid simulation to voxelize obstacles at every frame using low-poly meshes to minimize performance cost [S1, unofficial]. The technique evolved to include instancing for drawing multiple slices in a single draw call [S1, unofficial]. Later implementations, such as those in Cascaded [Voxel Cone Tracing](#1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md), utilized fragment shaders with structured buffers to write directly to voxel grids, handling reversed-Z architectures and precision issues via coordinate scaling [S2, unofficial].
